points.name: Half Dome
points.blurb: Rises about 4,800 feet above the Valley floor. Snake Dike climbs its southwest side.

points.name: Yosemite Falls
points.blurb: Drops 2,425 feet in three parts. It roars in late spring and can dry to a trickle by late summer.

points.name: El Capitan
points.blurb: About 3,000 feet of granite. The Nose was first climbed in 1958, after 47 days spread over 18 months.

points.name: Three Brothers
points.blurb: Three stacked summits on the north wall. The highest is Eagle Peak.

points.name: Royal Arches
points.blurb: Great stone arches above the Ahwahnee. The classic route up them is 16 pitches long.

points.name: North Dome
points.blurb: A granite dome on the north rim, looking across at Half Dome.

points.name: Sentinel Rock
points.blurb: A great spire on the south wall, about 3,000 feet above the floor.

points.name: Glacier Point
points.blurb: 7,214 feet. The Valley floor is 3,200 feet below. The Apron climb leads up to it.

points.name: Cathedral Rocks
points.blurb: Great buttresses on the south wall, beside Bridalveil Fall.

points.name: Vernal Fall
points.blurb: The Merced drops about 317 feet here, above Happy Isles.

points.name: Nevada Fall
points.blurb: The Merced drops about 594 feet, next to Liberty Cap.

points.name: Bridalveil Fall
points.blurb: Drops 620 feet and flows all year. On windy days its spray blows sideways.

points.name: Yosemite Village
points.blurb: The Welcome Center, store and museum. Camp 4 is a short walk west.

points.name: Lower Yosemite Fall
points.blurb: Lower Fall drops 320 feet. Above it are the middle cascades and Upper Fall.

points.name: Camp 4
points.blurb: Climbers have camped here since the 1950s. It joined the National Register in 2003.

points.name: Cook's Meadow
points.blurb: Open meadow under Yosemite Falls, good for foraging in season.

points.name: The Ahwahnee
points.blurb: Opened in 1927. Stone and concrete stained to look like redwood keep fire out.

points.name: Curry Village
points.blurb: David and Jennie Curry opened Camp Curry here in 1899 with just seven tents.

points.name: Lamon Homestead
points.blurb: Your camp, beside what is left of James Lamon’s 1860s apple orchard.

points.name: Happy Isles
points.blurb: The John Muir Trail starts here, about 211 miles from Mount Whitney.

points.name: Mirror Lake
points.blurb: Tenaya Creek forms a seasonal lake below Half Dome. By late summer it is often a meadow.

points.name: El Capitan Meadow
points.blurb: Open meadow at the foot of El Capitan, where climbers scan the wall.

points.name: Tunnel View
points.blurb: El Capitan on the left, Bridalveil Fall on the right, Half Dome beyond.
